audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed FY2025 noncontrolling-interest net income was $18m and adjusted EBITDA attributable to noncontrolling interest was $19m, 8.6% of the $221.5m anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Consolidated depreciation and other noncash add-backs may enter OE at 100% while net income and the share denominator represent only HGV stockholders; consolidated capital deductions could partly offset the mismatch.
audit_findings.evidence: Net income attributable to noncontrolling interest is the portion of Big Cedar that is attributable to Big Cedar Vacations, LLC, which holds the remaining 49% equity interest.
audit_findings.explanation: The 49% outside ownership of Big Cedar is demonstrated, but an OE basis error is only a possibility because the supplied record does not identify Big Cedar's depreciation, other add-backs, or capital deductions. The filed $19m non-parent EBITDA provides a relevant scale, but it is not the amount of any error, so materiality cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile every FY2025 OE add-back and deduction by legal entity, apply HGV's 51% economic share to Big Cedar items, and rerun all scenarios only if the resulting parent-attributable OE differs from $221.5m.

audit_findings.title: Finance and inventory growth may consume capital omitted from OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.038bn of filed FY2025 capital uses: $669m net increase in timeshare financing receivables plus $369m VOI inventory spending; comparable H1 2026 uses were $431m; normalized equity-funded requirement unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A normalized requirement for inventory development and receivable funding reduces distributable OE; securitization or warehouse proceeds finance assets but are not operating earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: Cash flows used in operating activities primarily include spending for the purchase and development of real estate for future conversion to inventory and funding our working capital needs.
audit_findings.explanation: Omission from the $221.5m anchor is not demonstrated because the OE reconstruction is not supplied. Nevertheless, the recurring filed capital uses are several times the anchor and are reasonably capable of changing every valuation scenario even after allowing for collections, inventory sales, and sustainable non-recourse financing.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild OE to show separately inventory purchases and development, receivable originations, collections, defaults, recoveries, and non-recourse funding. Estimate the normalized equity-funded maintenance requirement and rerun the valuation if it is absent from the anchor.

audit_findings.title: Temporary royalty discounts create future margin pressure
audit_findings.magnitude: incremental cost unquantified; filed Hilton license fees were $192m in FY2025 and total license-fee expense was $214m
audit_findings.mechanism: Contractual increases from discounted 2%-4% rates to 5%, plus any milestone surcharge, reduce forecast OE and terminal earnings rather than changing the historical anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: The reduced license fees range from 2% to 4% of the applicable gross revenue, increasing steadily until it reaches 5% during the fifth year and beyond for the Diamond Acquisition and during the fourth year and beyond for the Bluegreen Acquisition.
audit_findings.explanation: The contractual phase-in is demonstrated, but the record does not provide the applicable Diamond and Bluegreen revenue by current royalty rate, so the incremental annual cost and its materiality cannot be computed. Because the valuation projects beyond the phase-in dates, holding the FY2025 burden constant would overstate value.
audit_findings.action: Obtain acquisition-cohort gross revenue subject to each royalty rate, minimum-fee provisions, conversion dates, and milestone status; model the contractual annual fees and rerun the scenarios if those step-ups are not already included.

audit_findings.title: The latest-year anchor contains a large construction timing distortion
audit_findings.magnitude: $202m filed FY2025 net construction deferral, comprising $368m of sales, $105m of cost of sales and $61m of direct selling costs; deferred VOI sales reached $539m at June 30, 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Deferral shifts revenue and direct costs into completion periods while indirect selling costs remain in the current period, distorting the latest-actual OE anchor and subsequent growth base.
audit_findings.evidence: During the year ended December 31, 2025, we deferred $ 368 million of Sales of VOI, net related to projects under construction.
audit_findings.explanation: The timing distortion is demonstrated and the $202m net FY2025 amount equals 91.2% of the $221.5m anchor. It is plainly capable of changing the valuation. Direction is mixed because normalization could raise sustainable OE if projects complete at expected margins, but remaining completion costs, collectability, or weaker margins could reduce the benefit. H1 2026 recognized only $37m of sales while further deferrals increased the balance, so the issue remained open.
audit_findings.action: Create a project-level schedule of deferred revenue, deferred direct costs, indirect costs already expensed, remaining completion cash spending, expected recognition dates, and expected credit losses; derive normalized parent OE and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Favorable retrospective cost estimates boosted the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $40m pretax FY2025 favorable cost-of-sales true-up, equal to 18.1% of the $221.5m OE anchor; after-tax OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The favorable retrospective estimate revision lowers current cost of VOI sales and raises inventory, increasing latest-year earnings used in the OE anchor without necessarily representing recurring economics.
audit_findings.evidence: Costs of sales true-up decreased cost of VOI sales and increased inventory in all periods presented.
audit_findings.explanation: The $40m boost is demonstrated, not merely possible. Its pretax scale is large relative to the anchor and can change the valuation conclusion. Prior favorable true-ups of $23m in 2024 and $61m in 2023 show that true-ups recur, but they do not establish that the FY2025 benefit is sustainable or correctly represents current-period economics.
audit_findings.action: Separate the $40m true-up by project and assumption change, determine the parent-attributable after-tax portion arising from prior-period estimate revisions, establish a normalized recurring true-up if supported, and rerun the valuation using normalized OE.

audit_findings.title: Added cash may not all be distributable to the parent
audit_findings.magnitude: up to the $272m bridge addition, or $3.19 per fully diluted share; actual unavailable amount unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Restricted, pledged, trapped, subsidiary-level, or minimum operating cash should not be added as excess cash in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Our subsidiaries may not be able to, or may not be permitted to, make distributions to enable us to make payments in respect of our indebtedness.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that subsidiary distributions can be restricted, but it does not demonstrate that any specific portion of the $272m classified as cash and cash equivalents is unavailable. The bridge amount equals 8.0% of the $3.384bn base equity value, so a substantial exclusion could affect the conclusion, but the record cannot establish the unavailable portion or materiality.
audit_findings.action: Map the $272m by legal entity and account; identify covenant restrictions, pledges, regulatory or securitization limitations, taxes on transfer, and minimum operating cash; then rerun the equity bridge excluding only the evidenced unavailable amount.
